unit.title: More Letters of the Gurmukhi Alphabet

lesson.title: Finishing a Row: ਛ, ਜ, and ਝ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: You learned eleven letters last week, ending with ਚ (chachha)! Today we finish that same row with three more letters: ਛ (chhachha), ਜ (jajja), and ਝ (jhajha).

ਛ (chhachha) makes a breathier 'chh' sound than ਚ, pushed out with more air. ਜ (jajja) makes a 'j' sound, like in 'jam'. ਝ (jhajha) makes a breathier 'jh' sound, related to ਜ the same way ਛ is related to ਚ. Practice saying all four letters from this row together: cha... chha... ja... jha. Notice the pattern — every other letter is the 'breathier' version of the one before it.
You now know fourteen letters! This week we'll keep moving through new rows of the Gurmukhi alphabet.

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਛ (chhachha), ਜ (jajja), and ਝ (jhajha)
Notice the breathy/non-breathy pairing pattern between ਚ/ਛ and ਜ/ਝ
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's eleven letters, ending with ਚ.
2. Introduce ਛ, ਜ, ਝ one at a time, saying each name aloud together three times.
3. Practice the sound pattern: cha...chha...ja...jha, noticing the breathy pairing.
4. Trace each letter in the air before picking up a pencil.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter, then write it once more.
6. Close by counting all fourteen letters learned so far.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on ਜ (the clearest, most distinct sound) before adding ਛ and ਝ's breathier pairs
Ready for more: ask the child to identify which earlier letter (from last week) ਛ sounds most similar to, and why
This lesson deliberately skips ਞ (the row's fifth letter) — it did not pass this platform's Gurmukhi word-validation check, so it's held back rather than risked
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: ਛ, ਜ, ਝ complete the row begun with ਚ last week, continuing the systematic Painti Akhari sequence. Every letter was validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing.
